Loading the editing screen…

    Signing in with a Personal Access Token

    If the GitHub button gives you an error, or you would rather not use OAuth at all, paste a token below. The screen will reload with the token attached.

    Create a token at GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens → Generate new token. Choose Only select repositories and tick escape-the-bullshit, then under Repository permissions set Contents to Read and write. GitHub shows the token once. Keep it secret — treat it like a password.

    If the screen above does not come up

    Use the built-in local editor instead. It needs no internet connection, no GitHub account and no sign-in. It writes straight into your content files and rebuilds the site for you.

    Open the local editor

    First time here

    1. Check that admin/config.yml names your own GitHub repository in the repo line, and that the branch matches the one in the repository.
    2. Sign in with GitHub. You will be asked to allow access to that one repository only.
    3. Choose Pages or Topics from the list on the left.
    4. Pick a topic, change a sentence, and press Save.
    5. Back in your terminal, run npm run sync to pull the change down and rebuild.
    6. Reload the site in your browser to see it.

    Adding something new

    Press New at the top of the list. For Topics you get a labelled box for each section of an article; for Pages you get a title, a menu label and one large box for the page text. Fill it in and save — no other file needs changing.

    The address of a new page or article comes from the file name, which the editing screen creates from the title. Renaming the file later changes the address, so leave it alone once you have shared a link.

    About the wording

    Several pages cover health, dental and financial matters. They say plainly when a question needs a doctor, a dentist or a qualified adviser rather than a website. Please keep those notes in place when you rewrite a page — they matter for the reader and for the site's credibility.
